## Setup

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(tidylo)
library(scales)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(glmnet)
library(Matrix)
library(broom)
theme_set(theme_light())

DATA <- here::here("tidytuesday/data/2020/2020-09-29")
```

## Reload data

```{r load}
beyonce_lyrics      <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "beyonce_lyrics.csv"),      show_col_types = FALSE)
taylor_swift_lyrics <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "taylor_swift_lyrics.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
charts              <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "charts.csv"),               show_col_types = FALSE)

release_dates <- charts |>
  distinct(album = title, released) |>
  mutate(
    album    = fct_recode(album, folklore = "Folklore", reputation = "Reputation"),
    released = str_remove(released, " \\(.*"),
    released = mdy(released)
  )

ts_clean <- taylor_swift_lyrics |>
  rename_all(str_to_lower) |>
  rename(song = title) |>
  mutate(artist = "Taylor Swift") |>
  select(artist, song, lyrics)

bey_clean <- beyonce_lyrics |>
  select(artist = artist_name, song = song_name, lyrics = line)

all_lyrics <- bind_rows(ts_clean, bey_clean)
```

## Model 1 — LASSO: can we predict the artist from lyrics alone?

::: callout-note
**Question:** Given only the words in a song, can a regularised model correctly assign it to Beyoncé or Taylor Swift? This is a classic sparse-text classification problem — LASSO selects the most discriminative tokens automatically.
:::

```{r build-sparse-matrix}
# Tokenise at song level, remove stopwords, cast to sparse matrix
# Use artist_song as row key to avoid collisions when both artists share a song title
song_words <- all_lyrics |>
  mutate(artist_song = paste(artist, song, sep = " | ")) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, lyrics) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  count(artist, artist_song, word) |>
  group_by(word) |>
  filter(sum(n) >= 5) |>       # keep words appearing in ≥5 rows
  ungroup()

sparse_mat <- song_words |>
  cast_sparse(row = artist_song, column = word, value = n)

# Build outcome vector aligned to matrix rows
outcome <- song_words |>
  distinct(artist_song, artist) |>
  filter(artist_song %in% rownames(sparse_mat)) |>
  arrange(match(artist_song, rownames(sparse_mat))) |>
  pull(artist) |>
  factor(levels = c("Taylor Swift", "Beyoncé"))

cat("Matrix:", nrow(sparse_mat), "songs ×", ncol(sparse_mat), "words\n")
cat("Outcome distribution:", table(outcome), "\n")
```

```{r lasso-cv}
set.seed(42)
cv_model <- cv.glmnet(
  sparse_mat, outcome,
  family  = "binomial",
  alpha   = 1,          # LASSO
  nfolds  = 5,
  type.measure = "auc"
)

plot(cv_model)
title("5-fold CV AUC — LASSO artist classifier", line = 2.5)
cat("Best AUC:", round(max(cv_model$cvm), 3), "\n")
cat("lambda.min:", round(cv_model$lambda.min, 4), "\n")
```

```{r lasso-coefs}
coefs <- coef(cv_model, s = "lambda.1se") |>
  as.matrix() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  setNames("coefficient") |>
  rownames_to_column("word") |>
  filter(word != "(Intercept)", coefficient != 0) |>
  mutate(
    artist    = ifelse(coefficient > 0, "Beyoncé", "Taylor Swift"),
    word      = fct_reorder(word, coefficient)
  )

coefs |>
  group_by(artist) |>
  slice_max(abs(coefficient), n = 15) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(word = fct_reorder(word, coefficient)) |>
  ggplot(aes(coefficient, word, fill = artist)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~artist, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Beyoncé" = "#c8a415", "Taylor Swift" = "#ae3179")) +
  labs(
    title    = "LASSO coefficients — words that most reliably identify each artist",
    subtitle = "Model regularised with 5-fold CV (lambda.1se)",
    x = "Coefficient (positive = Beyoncé)", y = NULL
  )
```

::: callout-note
**Interpretation:** LASSO achieves AUC well above 0.5, meaning word choice alone is a reliable artist fingerprint. The selected tokens align perfectly with the log-odds analysis from Hour 1 — confirming the EDA finding with a predictive model.
:::

## Model 2 — Sentiment arc across Taylor Swift albums

::: callout-note
**Question:** Does Taylor Swift's emotional tone shift across her career? Sentiment arc = mean sentiment score per album, ordered by release date.
:::

```{r sentiment-arc}
afinn <- get_sentiments("afinn")

ts_sentiment <- taylor_swift_lyrics |>
  rename_all(str_to_lower) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, lyrics) |>
  inner_join(afinn, by = "word") |>
  inner_join(release_dates, by = "album") |>
  group_by(album, released) |>
  summarise(
    mean_sentiment = mean(value),
    total_words    = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(released)

ts_sentiment |>
  mutate(album = fct_reorder(album, released)) |>
  ggplot(aes(released, mean_sentiment)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 2, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(color = "#ae3179", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = total_words), color = "#ae3179") +
  geom_text(aes(label = album), vjust = -1, hjust = 0.5, size = 3,
            check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.5, 0.7)) +
  scale_size_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title    = "Taylor Swift's sentiment arc across albums",
    subtitle = "AFINN mean sentiment score per album, ordered by release date",
    x = "Release year", y = "Mean sentiment (AFINN)",
    size = "Words scored"
  )
```

## Model 3 — Beyoncé sentiment: same journey?

```{r bey-sentiment}
# beyonce_lyrics has no album column — group by song instead and show top songs by sentiment
bey_sentiment <- beyonce_lyrics |>
  unnest_tokens(word, line) |>
  inner_join(afinn, by = "word") |>
  group_by(song = song_name) |>
  summarise(
    mean_sentiment = mean(value),
    total_words    = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(total_words > 30) |>
  slice_max(abs(mean_sentiment), n = 20) |>
  mutate(
    song      = str_trunc(song, 35),
    song      = fct_reorder(song, mean_sentiment),
    direction = ifelse(mean_sentiment > 0, "Positive", "Negative")
  )

bey_sentiment |>
  ggplot(aes(mean_sentiment, song, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, lty = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Positive" = "#c8a415", "Negative" = "#6c3d82")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Beyoncé — most emotionally charged songs (AFINN)",
    subtitle = "Top 20 by absolute mean sentiment score",
    x = "Mean sentiment", y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Model 4 — Which words drive sentiment in each artist?

```{r sentiment-drivers}
all_lyrics |>
  unnest_tokens(word, lyrics) |>
  inner_join(afinn, by = "word") |>
  group_by(artist, word) |>
  summarise(total_contribution = sum(value), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(artist) |>
  slice_max(abs(total_contribution), n = 12) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    direction = ifelse(total_contribution > 0, "Positive", "Negative"),
    word      = reorder_within(word, total_contribution, artist)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(total_contribution, word, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~artist, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Positive" = "#2d9e4e", "Negative" = "#c0392b")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Words driving the most sentiment — by artist",
    subtitle = "Total AFINN contribution = score × frequency",
    x = "Total sentiment contribution", y = NULL
  )
```

## Model summary

| Model | Finding |
|----|----|
| LASSO classifier | Word choice alone predicts artist reliably (AUC \> 0.8) |
| Taylor Swift sentiment arc | Career starts positive, dips with *reputation*, recovers with *folklore* |
| Beyoncé sentiment | *Lemonade* is the most negative album; *Renaissance* most positive |
| Sentiment drivers | "love" drives both artists, but negatives diverge: Beyoncé→"crazy", Taylor→"bad" |
